gloss: to bite one's lip (in frustration or regret)

definitions.gloss: to bite one's lip; to feel frustrated; to feel deep regret
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression describing the feeling of frustration, vexation, or bitter regret, often when one cannot express their feelings openly or must suppress an emotional reaction.

examples.japanese: {悔|くや}しくて{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}んだ。
examples.english: I bit my lip in frustration.

examples.japanese: {言|い}い{返|かえ}せず、{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}むしかなかった。
examples.english: Unable to talk back, I could only bite my lip.

examples.japanese: あの{時|とき}もっと{頑張|がんば}ればよかったと、{今|いま}でも{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}む{思|おも}いだ。
examples.english: Even now I feel bitter regret, wishing I had tried harder back then.

notes:
IDIOM STRUCTURE:
{唇|くちびる} (lip) + を + {噛|か}む (to bite)

The expression describes the physical action of biting one's lip as a metaphor for suppressing emotions, particularly frustration or regret.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{悔|くや}しくて{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}む - bite one's lip in frustration
・{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}む{思|おも}い - bitter feelings of regret
・{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}みしめる - to bite down hard on one's lip (intensified form)

NUANCE:
Always indicates negative emotions - frustration, regret, helplessness, or suppressed anger. Often implies the person cannot openly express their feelings or take action.

VARIATION:
{唇|くちびる}を{噛|か}みしめる is a more intense version, suggesting even stronger suppression of emotion.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
・{歯|は}を{食|く}いしばる - to grit one's teeth (endurance)
・{拳|こぶし}を{握|にぎ}る - to clench one's fist (determination/frustration)
・{涙|なみだ}を{呑|の}む - to swallow one's tears (accept disappointment)

REGISTER:
Neutral. Common in both spoken and written Japanese, especially in dramatic or emotional contexts.
